newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia crude, condensate output seen higher.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia crude, condensate output seen higher.

text.p: Australia's official commodity forecaster on Tuesday retained its production forecast for crude oil and condensate at 9.1 percent growth in 1996/97 (July/June) to 33 billion litres, or 570,000 barrels per day (bdp).

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics' (ABARE) latest forceast compares with projected national output of 30.3 billion litres in 1995/96 and largely attributed the increase to new oil fields coming on stream.

"Significant contributors will be the 45,000 barrels a day of new capacity to come on stream from the Gippsland basin and approximately 150,000 barrels a day of additional capacity from the Carnarvon basin," ABARE said in its September report.
It also assumed the Wanaea-Cossack oil field on the North West Shelf, the only area to show any output growth in 1995/96, would approach peak production in calendar 1997, ABARE said.
Australian exports of crude oil and condensate are forecast to rise by 19.3 percent to 13 billion litres (224,000 bpd) in 1996/97 and be worth A$2.1 billion, ABARE said.

It also retained its forecast of 4.9 percent growth in natural gas production to 32.3 billion cubic metres in 1996/97 and said export volumes would be flat at 7.48 billion cubic metres but be worth 9.3 percent more at A$1.5 billion due to a forecast five percent increase in the unit export price.
"In the LNG market, the North West Shelf joint ventures have announced that their Japanese buyers are interested in taking an additonal 6.8 million tonnes a year from 2003," the report said.
"To meet this demand, Australian gas production capacity will need to increase to around 14.5 million tonnes a year."
Primary liquefied petroleum gas production was expected to increase 37 percent to five billion litres in 1996/97, consistent with the previous forecast.
Refinery production was forecast to rise 1.6 percent.
